content: Hives, also known as urticaria, may occur as a reaction to digoxin. Symptoms such as nausea or vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting can also manifest. Stomach cramps and joint pain are additional potential side effects. Changes in heart rate or rhythm, including bradycardia (a slower-than-normal heart rate), may occur. Digoxin can also lead to irregular heart rhythms, which may result in fainting. In rare cases, this can cause the heart to suddenly stop beating, a condition known as cardiac arrest. Individuals with pre-existing heart disease or those taking other medications that affect the heart are at a higher risk for these complications. If you experience symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, or changes in heart rate or rhythm (e.g., fast, slow, pounding, or skipping beats), you should inform your healthcare provider immediately. Other concerning symptoms include confusion, weakness, or fatigue. Digoxin toxicity can occur if there is an excessive amount of the drug in your body. Symptoms of digoxin toxicity include loss of appetite, persistent nausea or vomiting, diarrhea, confusion, weakness, changes in vision, and abnormal heart rhythms (arrhythmias). If you suspect digoxin toxicity, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additional medical tests may be required to confirm the diagnosis. Certain individuals should not use digoxin. This includes those allergic to digoxin, digitalis, Lanoxin, or any ingredients in the specific product. People with a type of abnormal heart rhythm called ventricular fibrillation should also avoid digoxin. Before using digoxin, ensure it has been prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have similar conditions, as it may harm them. Keep digoxin out of reach of children. Be aware that digoxin can affect your alertness and coordination, so avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring these skills until you know how the medication affects you. Digoxin may also influence your blood pressure and heart rate, so discuss symptom monitoring with your healthcare provider. If you are prescribed digoxin oral solution, use the provided oral syringe to measure your dose accurately. Consult your pharmacist if you are unsure how to measure your dose. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This will help determine if digoxin is appropriate for you. Specifically, discuss conditions such as Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, sinus node disease, atrioventricular (AV) block, kidney problems, myocarditis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, thyroid issues, chronic diarrhea, or electrolyte imbalances (e.g., low potassium, magnesium, or calcium levels, or high calcium levels). If you are undergoing a medical procedure like electrical cardioversion, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking digoxin. Additionally, digoxin may interact with other medications and supplements, so provide a complete list of what you are using to your healthcare provider. The absorption of oral digoxin may be reduced if taken with meals high in bran fiber. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects digoxin, but drinking alcohol while on digoxin may increase the risk of dizziness, blurred vision, and confusion. In the event of an overdose, stop taking digoxin and seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Digoxin is commonly used to treat heart failure, a condition where the heart does not pump blood effectively. It is also used to manage chronic atrial fibrillation, a condition where the upper and lower chambers of the heart do not work together, leading to an irregular heartbeat. Digoxin strengthens heart contractions and improves blood flow while helping to control heart rate. Digoxin works by inhibiting the sodium-potassium ATPase pump in the heart, which increases the force of heart contractions and lowers the heart rate. It is available as an oral solution, tablets, or injectable forms. Store digoxin at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) and protect it from extreme temperatures. Keep it in a cool, dry place. Common side effects of digoxin include changes in heart rate or rhythm, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, blurry or yellow/green vision, headache, weakness, dizziness, confusion, anxiety, depression, hallucinations, enlarged breasts in men, and rash. If you experience any bothersome side effects, contact your healthcare provider. Serious allergic reactions, such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or severe skin reactions, require immediate medical attention.
